predecessors.name: Avar Khaganate
predecessors.text: the Slavs who revolted 'in 623-24', 'assumed originally subject to Avar rulers (kagans)'

successors.name: Carantania
successors.text: 'A smaller part of the original March of the Slavs, centred north of modern Klagenfurt, preserved independence'

successors.name: Avar Khaganate
successors.text: 'the Avars returned to their earlier territories, at least southernmost modern Slovakia'

ledger.x: c. 623: the Frankish merchant Samo becomes the Slavs' king in their revolt against the Avars. 'According to Fredegar, Samo, a Frankish merchant, went to the Slavs in c. 623-624'; he became king 'during a revolt of 623-24'. The page gives no capital and no boundary…
631: after Wogastisburg Dervan's Sorbs join Samo.
658: Samo dies and the tribal union breaks up; the Alpine Slavs keep their independence.
658: the Avars return to the south of the former realm.
658: the realm's core falls apart into tribes.

wars.name: Slavic revolt against the Avars
wars.outcome: The page has Samo become king 'during a revolt of 623-24' or after the Avar defeat of 626; the Carantania page says 626 'brought an end to Avar dominance over Slavs, as the Avars were defeated at Constantinople'.

wars.name: Battle of Wogastisburg
wars.outcome: Dagobert I led three armies of 'Alamanni, Lombards, and Austrasian Franks'; 'the main fighting force was defeated in a three-day siege' (Slavic victory, 'Enlargement of Samo's realm').

wars.name: Samo's raids on Thuringia
wars.outcome: Samo 'raided Frankish Thuringia several times after the battle'; Dervan fought Thuringia 631-634 and was defeated by Radulf in 636; 'In 641, the rebellious Radulf sought an alliance with Samo against his sovereign, Sigebert III'.

certainty.note: The page: 'The extent of Samo's power before and after 631 is disputed'; no capital, no treaty line, no survey.
